thread:
Maria: paging P1 - multiple inference pods restarting on gpu-node-07, customers reporting 503s for a subset of endpoints. getting pages from prod alerts. I’m on it.

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert created (PD-1421). Severity P1 - GPU node instability (gpu-node-07). Notifying on-call.

Samir: acked. jumping in. any recent deploys?

Jules: no prod deploys in the last 3h, CI shows nothing. I can run a quick node check.

Samir: can you paste the pod statuses? suspect OOM / container crashloop or driver reset.

Jules: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-07`
```
Jules: INFERENCE-23   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  0  24m  gpu-node-07  3.2GB / 16GB
Jules: INFERENCE-18   0/1 Error            0  25m  gpu-node-07  OOMKilled
Jules: routing-proxy   1/1 Running        3d  gpu-node-07  512MB / 2GB
```

Elaine: pulling dmesg and nvidia logs from node. attaching snippets.

Elaine: /var/log/kern.log excerpt:
```
Elaine: [ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI-MSG) 79: GPU at 0000:03:00.0: PID 12345: out of memory
Elaine: [ 12345.679002] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Elaine: [ 12345.679123] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (inference-run) total-vm: ...
```

Elaine: /var/log/nvidia-installer.log / dmesg shows repeated "GPU has fallen off the bus" and a couple of ECC RAS messages: "GPU RAS: uncorrectable ECC".

Samir: OK that's a driver/board-level fault, not just container OOM. can we cordon and drain the node? need to get traffic off ASAP.

Maria: Customer-impact: CS reported increased 503s for small set of customers hitting model-route `/v1/generate/redwood-large`. Tagged 6 customers so far. Notifying them (CS on it).

customer-success: we’ve messaged the affected customers and provided temporary mitigation steps (retry/backoff) and ETA ~60m. asked if they want failover to hosted pool.

Samir: Plan: 1) cordon gpu-node-07 2) kubectl drain (ignore-daemonsets) 3) move affected pods to fallback pool (route via LB) 4) reboot node + reinstall driver if needed 5) monitor.

Jules: running commands now:
```
Jules: kubectl cordon gpu-node-07
Jules: kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

Jules: drain started; some pods stuck due to local stateful services, forcing delete for inference pods.

Samir: while that's happening, create temp routing rule to send /v1/generate/redwood-large to dedicated fallback pool (gpu-fallback-pool) to reduce customer impact.

Maria: done, routing rule applied via API gateway. should start seeing failover in the next 30s.

infra-bot: Load balancer update applied: route `redwood-large` -> `gpu-fallback-pool`.

Jules: node cordoned and drained. pods evacuated. node now in NotReady state post-drain, kernel reports GPU fell off the bus and NV driver shows repeated Xid 79 and Xid 31 messages.

Elaine: trying driver restart: `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` then `modprobe -r nvidia_uvm && modprobe nvidia_uvm` but initial attempts fail with: `NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus` and `rm_init: failed`.

Samir: reboot the host. if the driver can’t reattach the device, OS-level reboot is quickest. schedule a 10-min reboot.

Maria: taking the reboot window now. notifying CS update.

Jules: reboot issued (`sudo reboot`) at 1768457075.

incident-bot: Reboot initiated for gpu-node-07. Expected downtime ~5-10m for node.

Elaine: post-reboot logs: one GPU fails to reinitialize, kernel shows persistent ECC errors on GPU0. suspect hardware fault on GPU0 (board/PCIe).

Samir: node back up but kubelet marks node Ready with taint `GPU-failed=true:NoSchedule`. I manually added the taint to prevent scheduling until we replace or fully test.

Jules: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows gpu-node-07 Ready but tainted, other nodes absorbing load. No more CrashLoopBackOff for evacuated pods. Traffic to affected endpoints down to normal for most customers.

Maria: CS notified customers that we mitigated via failover and we're replacing faulty hardware; offering scalability credits for impacted windows.

Elaine: hardware ticket opened with cloud provider (case 88922). provider suggested RMA for the GPU; we've requested expedited swap.

Samir: follow-up actions for P1: - replace GPU on node or move workloads permanently off this host - add more aggressive node-level health check for NV driver flapping - add automatic temporary routing to fallback pool on driver reset alerts - improve on-call runbook to include cordon/drain/reboot pattern for GPU RAS errors.

Maria: handing off to Samir for overnight monitoring. I’ll annotate the incident timeline and start the PM draft.

Samir: taking over. will keep watch for 2h and confirm RMA once provider updates. leaving node tainted and cordoned.

incident-bot: PD-1421 status changed to "acknowledged" -> "in progress".

infra-bot: autoscaler adjusted to add 2 extra fallback nodes for the cluster to absorb load (scale-up triggered).

customer-success: customers acknowledged the mitigation and appreciate the proactive routing. one asked for a brief postmortem. scheduled postmortem for tomorrow 11:00 PT.

Jules: collecting logs/stack traces for postmortem, exporting dmesg / var/log/nvidia* / kubelet logs and attaching to the incident ticket.

Elaine: snippet for postmortem:
```
Elaine: Root cause (prelim): GPU0 on gpu-node-07 experienced uncorrectable ECC/RAS fault leading to repeated driver resets (Xid 79/31). kernel OOMs triggered container restarts. Mitigation: cordon/drain/reboot, route traffic to fallback pool, open RMA with provider.
```

Samir: Great. I’ll update runbook with a section for persistent GPU RAS errors. If provider confirms hardware failure we’ll schedule replacement during maintenance window.

Maria: thanks all. handing off completed at 1768461402.

incident-bot: PD-1421 updated to "monitoring". Follow-up: create postmortem and link to incident ticket PD-1421.
